editorial.headline: A Boxing Club Is Open Nationally—But Not to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Boxing clubs may be nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet Bali’s OSS scale gate prevents PT PMA registration for this activity.
editorial.body:
**A boxing club is a membership organisation, not merely a place with a ring.** This activity covers professional, semi-professional and amateur boxing clubs that give members the opportunity to take part in sport. The defining function is the club and its members’ participation; premises and sporting facilities may be provided, but they are not a condition of the activity. That distinction matters because the description encompasses a club operating a venue as well as one organising participation without supplying a dedicated training space. It is an organisational activity built around boxing membership across professional, semi-professional and amateur settings.

Nationally, the activity is listed as open to foreign investment, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. Yet its ordinary business-scale opening is limited to Mikro and Kecil. For a founder, this establishes the formal national posture clearly: the activity may be organised around participation at those named scales, while the foreign-investment setting does not reduce the ownership ceiling below full foreign ownership. The recorded national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

In Bali, the answer is materially different and should be read without euphemism: a foreigner cannot register this activity through a PT PMA today. The Bali record marks it CHIUSO_PMA_NO_BESAR because the OSS system has no Usaha Besar scale row for the activity. Its available scale rows are Mikro, Kecil and Menengah; a PT PMA is treated as Besar by law, so the OSS-RBA scale gate bars it. The recorded verification is from June 2026 and cites PP 28/2025, Article 127. The national 100% ceiling therefore does not create a Bali registration route for PMA.

The province’s broader moratorium rule reinforces the restrictive environment: Bali blocks PMA island-wide and permanently across Low and Medium-Low risk activities, under Governor’s letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. That wider rule does not alter the precise reason recorded here. The decisive point for this club activity is the absence of an Usaha Besar OSS row, which makes national openness unavailable to PT PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness and a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling do not create a PMA registration route in Bali.
